comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C153-C156 regarding FAP mechanisms affecting NMJ development. Both evaluations rate these as UNCERTAIN/speculative, noting the lack of direct experimental validation for proposed juxtacrine/paracrine signaling mechanisms and Hsd11b1-positive FAP populations.

Strong agreement on claims C42-C48 describing severe phenotype of SMN2 0-copy mutants. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on photographic and histological evidence, while peer reviewers accepted these basic phenotypic observations without question as part of establishing the model system.

Significant disagreement on claims C123-C126 regarding FAP transplantation rescue. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing localized rescue as strong evidence for causality. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting 'rescue data were not convincing,' incomplete functional recovery, and need for additional experimentation.

Agreement on claims C82-C85 validating conditional knockout specificity. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes qRT-PCR and genomic PCR validation, while peer reviewers accepted the genetic characterization as convincing with novel conditional approaches.

Agreement on claims C86-C90 establishing dose-dependent relationship between SMN levels and phenotype. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights western blot data, while peer reviewers accepted the gene dosage-dependence demonstration as part of genetic characterization.

Disagreement on claims C49-C59 describing bone phenotype of SMN2 1-copy mutants. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on micro-CT and histological data. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, stating 'skeletal analyses are not rigorous' and work is 'descriptive in nature,' unable to 'satisfactorily elucidate SMN regulation of bone development.'

Disagreement on claims C60-C64 describing growth plate defects. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on H&E staining and Ki67 immunostaining showing reduced zone lengths and decreased proliferation. Peer reviewers include these in UNCERTAIN evaluation, citing lack of mechanistic rigor in skeletal analyses.

Disagreement on claims C65-C79 regarding local IGF deficiency mechanism. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, calling it a 'key mechanistic finding.' Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, stating work is 'descriptive' and 'skeletal analyses were not rigorous,' suggesting IGF mechanism needs further validation.

Disagreement on claims C137-C138 synthesizing bone findings. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, concluding bone defects are cell-autonomous. Peer reviewers include these in UNCERTAIN evaluation, noting inability to satisfactorily elucidate mechanisms and need for more rigorous analyses.

Agreement on claims C91-C98 describing NMJ maturation defects at P21. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes immunostaining data and interpretation of neurogenic vs. physiologic atrophy. Peer reviewers praised NMJ characterization as 'relatively strong' with 'convincing' data.

Agreement on claims C99-C102 establishing temporal progression of NMJ defects. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes P3 immunostaining data supports juvenile stage emergence. Peer reviewers accepted NMJ characterization as convincing part of genetic evidence.

Agreement on claims C103-C108 describing progressive NMJ morphology worsening in adults. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights dose-dependent effects in quantification. Peer reviewers affirmed the work demonstrates copy number influence on NMJ structure.

Agreement on claims C109-C115 describing functional NMJ defects. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes electrophysiological evidence for decreased quantal content mechanism. Peer reviewers found genetic evidence for NMJ abnormalities convincing.

Agreement on claims C116-C122 describing ultrastructural NMJ defects. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes TEM data showing increased vesicle density and nerve terminal detachment. Peer reviewers accepted NMJ characterization as part of convincing genetic evidence.

Agreement on claims C127-C136 synthesizing NMJ findings. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comparison to prior SMA models and transplantation rescue support. Peer reviewers consistently praised NMJ characterization and confirmed work advances understanding of SMN's role.

Disagreement on claims C143-C146 presenting major conclusions. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on dose-dependent effects and FAP rescue. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, finding therapeutic implications premature given mechanistic gaps and incomplete rescue data.

Disagreement on claims C147-C152 discussing therapy limitations. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on citations and reasonable inferences. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, stating additional experimentation needed to justify conclusions and noting descriptive nature weakens therapeutic recommendations.

OpenEval evaluated claims C1-C23 as SUPPORTED background knowledge about SMA with established literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory/background claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C24-C30 as SUPPORTED prior work on peripheral SMN importance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature review claims establishing study rationale.
OpenEval evaluated claims C31-C37 as SUPPORTED knowledge gap regarding bone growth defects. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims establishing study rationale.
OpenEval evaluated claims C38-C41 as SUPPORTED biological context for FAPs and knowledge gap. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory claims.
